audit.why: The content chart gives Aatrox five of seven stages, which matches the mirror at audits/top/tahmkench__aatrox.json and Aatrox's 51.39% over 1835 games. Left untouched so the two directions stay aligned.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] and mid both treat level 6 as the arrival of Tahm Kench's repositioning tool ('Tahm R Devour/Abyssal gives him an escape valve'). His blink has existed since level 2.
audit.why: Abyssal Dive is his W, cooldown 21/20/19/18/17, live from level 2 — that is the escape and the knockup, and it is why levels 2-5 are not free. The level-6 arrival is Devour, a single committed removal on a 120s cooldown, not an escape hatch.
audit.corrected: Escape attributed to Abyssal Dive (W, 21s) from level 2; level 6 reframed around Devour as a one-shot 120s removal.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two errors. First, late says Devour 'lets him eat himself out of a combo' — Devour targets a champion to damage an enemy or shield an ally; his self-escape is Abyssal Dive. Second, wants.foe[0] sells '3 Q stacks for the stun, then W leap' as a combo, but three stacks of An Acquired Taste are spent EITHER on the Tongue Lash stun OR on Devour, never both.
audit.why: Riot's text: An Acquired Taste — 'At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion'; Devour — 'Tahm Kench devours a champion for a few seconds, dealing magic damage if they are an enemy, or shielding them if they are an ally'; Abyssal Dive — 'Dive down and then re-appear at target location, damaging and knocking up all enemies in an area.' Abyssal Dive is both his only gap-close and his only escape, on 21/20/19/18/17, so the whole lane is played on that one timer.
audit.corrected: Devour corrected to an enemy-or-ally cast on a 120s cooldown; the stun and the eat presented as an either/or spend of the same three stacks; Abyssal Dive named as the 21s window that decides when you commit.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry's whole plan is 'out-DPS his regen' and it never names Grievous Wounds.
audit.why: Thick Skin stores a share of the damage he takes and converts it to healing or a shield on a 3s cooldown, and An Acquired Taste scales his damage off his total health — so the longer you hit him the more he heals, and every point of HP you buy makes him hit harder. Anti-heal is not optional here; it is the item that makes the attrition plan work.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds stated in spikes[2].text in place of the vague 'keep hitting him' line.

edits.before: Tahm R Devour/Abyssal gives him an escape valve, but your World Ender heal-amp still out-drains his Grey Health — commit while his W is down and you win the all-in on raw damage.
edits.after: Abyssal Dive (21s) has been his escape and his gap-close since level 2 — commit in the window it is down. Devour at 6 is one 120s removal, not an escape hatch he can self-cast.

edits.before: Your bruiser spike plus full Q pattern out-DPS his Grey-Health regen; keep hitting him so his passive shield never refills between trades.
edits.after: Your bruiser spike plus full Q pattern out-DPS his regen, but Thick Skin banks a slice of all you land — buy Grievous Wounds first.

edits.before: Levels 2-5 are your window. Dodge his Q so the stun never lands, then punch him with Q3 sweetspot into W Infernal Chains and drain — your continuous damage out-paces his Grey-Health regen, which only heals when he isn't being hit. Keep the pressure constant so his passive shield never refills. He has no gap-close on you besides W, so once his W is down you control every trade through this whole stretch, and at 6 your R heal-amp still out-drains him even though his R gives an escape.
edits.after: Levels 2-5 are your window. Dodge Tongue Lash so his stacks never reach three, then punch him with Q3 sweetspot into Infernal Chains and drain — your continuous damage out-paces Thick Skin, which banks a share of everything you land and pays it back to him out of combat. His only gap-close and his only escape are the same 21s Abyssal Dive, so count that one timer and commit the moment it is spent. At 6 World Ender still out-drains him.

edits.before: Tahm's level-6 R is his relief valve: Devour lets him eat himself out of a combo, so don't over-commit expecting a clean kill — but your World Ender heal-amp still wins the damage race. Past that, your first-item bruiser spike and full Q pattern out-DPS his regen, and in an extended 1v1 your drain simply outlasts him — keep hitting so Grey Health never converts. His late value is using R to disengage or flank rather than duel you, so translate your lane lead into pressure before fights spread out.
edits.after: Tahm's level-6 Devour is a 120s commitment on a single champion — damage on you, a shield on an ally — and not a self-escape, so he cannot eat his way out of your combo. Your World Ender heal amp still wins the damage race. Past that, your first-item bruiser spike and full Q pattern out-DPS his regen, and in an extended 1v1 your drain outlasts him provided Grievous Wounds is down. His late value is peeling a carry off you rather than duelling, so translate the lane lead before fights spread out.

edits.before: Land 3 Q stacks for the stun, then W leap
edits.after: Spend 3 stacks: Tongue Lash stun or Devour

edits.before: Use R to escape or disengage a losing brawl
edits.after: Blink clear on his 21s Abyssal Dive first

edits.before: Tahm Kench changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Tahm Q, passive stacks, E shield, and R. Aatrox wins by controlling spacing with his first two Q swings, holding E until the enemy punish tool is committed, and managing the wave so the enemy must walk into the outer edge of his Q. Tahm Kench wants to survive lane, farm safely, stack durability, and become more valuable in later fights than the early lane suggests.
edits.after: Tahm Kench changes the lane by forcing Aatrox to respect Tongue Lash stacking An Acquired Taste, which he spends on either the stun or on Devour but never on both, and Thick Skin banking a share of the damage Aatrox lands. Aatrox wins by committing in the window while the 21s Abyssal Dive is spent, spacing with his first two Darkin Blade swings, and buying Grievous Wounds before any long fight.

notes: Mirror audits/top/tahmkench__aatrox.json reused wholesale for the mechanical findings and its warnings are confirmed from this side: (1) the kit file lists Devour's cooldown as 0 and range as 25000 — Data Dragon placeholders; the mirror gives 120/100/80 and 250, which is what I used; (2) 'Abyssal Voyage' is a removed pre-rework ultimate that still appears ~182 times in champ-data/content/tahmkench.js; the Aatrox side does not use that name but does treat the blink as a level-6 ultimate, which I corrected; (3) the 3-stack 'stun into Devour' combo is impossible and appears across the file. This matchup's Aatrox-side text is consistent with the mirror after these edits. Additional correction: the Teemo mirror (audits/top/teemo__aatrox.json) is right that Infernal Chains' 'grounding' flag in champ-data/_kits/aatrox.json is unsupported by Riot's description — the W drags lingering targets to the centre, it does not ground. I removed a grounding claim from this proposal before writing it.
